i8pvu: Team: after Monday's meeting, I want to clarify what was decided and what is still pending. The client confirms that the presentation will be on Friday; he has not asked us to finish all the tests by then. That difference matters. If we promise a final version, the technical team will have to work at night and, even so, will not be able to guarantee that it works on all devices. I propose that we show a prototype and explain its limits clearly. I don't consider it acceptable to pass on to the client a certainty that we don't yet have.
129aprq: Lucía insists that she has two people available to review the data. Tomás, on the other hand, insists that we assign a third person to design. Both statements seem incompatible only if we assume that all tasks must be done at the same time. I suggest that Lucía finish the figures first and that Tomás get support afterward. I need each person responsible to say, before Wednesday, what they can deliver without compromising quality. No one has to justify their personal circumstances publicly; it is enough to state their availability and the dependencies of their work.
c9yp1g: It is also worth reviewing how we ask for help. During the meeting it was repeated that the team should get more involved, but it was not specified who would do what. An invitation that general can seem kind and turn out to be of little use. I prefer a precise request that allows negotiation to a demand disguised as enthusiasm. For my part, I will handle the conversation with the client and communicate any change of scope. I ask you not to accept new tasks without first checking their effect on the deadlines already agreed.
1bvb6w9: On Thursday we will check progress. If a blocker appears, we will record it together with an alternative, without looking for someone to blame. The aim of this email is to distribute decisions as well as work: coordinating well does not mean being available at all hours, but knowing what each person expects and what they can expect from the others.
